body.statement:
Let \(k_{\mathrm{alg}}\geq 1\).  If an ideal over a field in \(k_{\mathrm{alg}}\) indeterminates is generated by polynomials of total degree at most three, then, for every admissible monomial order, every element of its reduced Gr\"obner basis has total degree at most
\[
 \left\lfloor
 2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^{2^{k_{\mathrm{alg}}-1}}
 \right\rfloor.
\]

source.locator: Corollary 8.3, specialized to generating degree three
source.verbatim_statement: Let F be a subset of K[X], I the ideal generated by F, and let d be the maximum degree of any f in F. Then for any admissible ordering, the degree of polynomials required in a Groebner basis for I is bounded by 2((d^2/2)+d)^(2^(n-1)).

attestation.note: Verified against Dubé 1990, Corollary 8.3, in the SIAM publisher record and the complete author-hosted PDF at University of Waterloo; substituting d=3 yields the cited general cubic bound, with the floor harmless because basis degrees are integers.
